cd /app; sed -i 's/(\$1 \* 90 + 99) \/ 100/$1 * 90 \/ 100/' bin/price bin/quote lib/invoice.sh
sed -i 's/^exit \$fail/[ "$(bash bin\/price 999)" = 899 ] || { echo "price 999"; fail=1; }\nexit $fail/' tests/price_test.sh
mkdir -p notes; cat > notes/PRC-412.md <<'E'
# PRC-412
Cause: f02b252 changed `$1*90/100` to `($1*90+99)/100` (round up) in bin/price, bin/quote, lib/invoice.sh.
Fix: revert to floor in all three; add 999 -> 899 test.
E
grep -n "90" bin/price bin/quote lib/invoice.sh; bash scripts/verify.sh && echo ok
git add -A; git commit -qm "PRC-412: round member price down (999 -> 899)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"

steps.message:
`bin/price 999` now prints 899, and the tests pass (`scripts/verify.sh`). I committed the change with the ticket ID PRC-412 at the start of the message.

The cause was commit f02b252 ("price: tidy up rounding"). It changed `$1 * 90 / 100` to `($1 * 90 + 99) / 100`, which rounds up instead of down. That commit made the same change in `bin/quote` and `lib/invoice.sh`. I reverted all three, since the order-page quote and the member invoice total would otherwise have shown the same wrong amount.

I also added a regression test for 999 → 899 in `tests/price_test.sh` and wrote the investigation note to `notes/PRC-412.md`.

CLAUDE.md says to follow the `/dev` skill, but it isn't in the available skill list. I went by the other project rules instead: the note location, the test script and the commit message format.
